items.item: g = 2 means every new chunk is larger than the sum of every chunk freed before it, so the vector can never reuse its own discarded memory

items.item: reserve(n) is a directive, not a resize: it reallocates iff current capacity < n, and prevents further reallocation until the reserved capacity would be exceeded

at.step: Reserve skips the early resizes

items.item: shrink_to_fit() is explicitly non-binding in the standard: it may do nothing at all and remain correct

items.item: whether a pointer survives a call to reserve or shrink_to_fit depends entirely on whether that specific call actually reallocated, not on which function was called

items.item: a contiguous array lets one cache-line fetch serve several elements; a pointer-chased structure can cost one cache line per element, which the next topic measures

items.item: CPython's list over-allocates far more gently than either g = 2 or g = 1.5, trading many more, smaller reallocations for far less wasted capacity at any given moment
